title: Raspberry leaf tincture
subtitle: A long-course tincture of Rubus idaeus leaf for the uterine toning traditionally used in late pregnancy preparation
excerpt: Raspberry leaf tincture is a 1:5 extract of dried raspberry leaf in 40% spirit, prepared as a uterine tonic traditionally taken in the last trimester of pregnancy under herbalist guidance, or for menstrual irregularity and cramping outside pregnancy. A 100 ml bottle holds about 20 doses at 5 ml. Keeps two years in a cool dark cupboard.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), raspberry entry, Botanical.com. Felter & Lloyd, King's American Dispensatory (1898), Rubus idaeus entry. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Rubus idaeus, folium (2013, EMA/HMPC/44842/2012), open access.

glossaryTerms.definition: A herb traditionally used to support the tone and function of the uterus, taken over weeks to support regular, comfortable menstrual cycles, or in the traditional western herbal use as a preparatory herb in late pregnancy.

projectSchedule.title: Start maceration
projectSchedule.body: Weigh 20 g of dried raspberry leaf into a clean jar. Pour over 100 ml of 40% spirit. Seal and label with the date.

projectSchedule.title: Strain and bottle
projectSchedule.body: Strain through muslin into a dark glass bottle. The tincture will be a pale olive-green or light amber. Label with the herb, spirit percentage, and date.

content.text: Raspberry leaf herbal extract is a gentle extract of dried Rubus idaeus leaf in 40% spirit, macerating for 4 to 6 weeks. A traditional

, long prepared in European home herbal practice for menstrual irregularity and mild cramping, and with a well-known but nuanced traditional use in the last weeks of pregnancy under midwife or herbalist guidance. The taste is mild, slightly astringent, with a faint fruitiness. A 100 ml bottle holds about 20 doses at 5 ml.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

content.text: Weigh 20 g of dried raspberry leaf into a clean steeping jar. Pour 100 ml of 40% spirit over the leaf. Seal tightly and label with the herb name and date.
Store in a cool dark place for 4 to 6 weeks, shaking every few days.
Strain through doubled muslin into a dark glass bottle. Press the leaf to extract as much liquid as possible. Label and store in a cool dark cupboard.

For menstrual support: 3 to 5 ml in a small glass of water, twice daily from mid-cycle. Take for 3 months and reassess. For late-pregnancy use: dose and timing as directed by your midwife or herbalist, do not use outside professional supervision.
Sealed dark glass bottle in a cool dark cupboard. Keeps two years from the date of straining.
When not to use this remedy

Do not take in the first or second trimester of pregnancy without specialist guidance. See a doctor for any new change in your menstrual cycle, bleeding between periods, or a major change in cycle length. These need a specialist check rather than herbal management.
